text:
ana: Heads up — after the maintenance window last night I saw a cluster of G2 nodes in us-west-2 throw intermittent Xid 61/65 after cold reboots. Happens within 10–30 minutes of boot and usually coincides with a network-heavy shuffle from the scheduler. Can repro on 3 different racks.

cheng: ugh. any kernel logs or nvml dumps?

ana: pasted a short dmesg snippet below — pattern looks like PCIe link reset then an xid. Not the usual thermal ramp.

ana: ```
[  120.345678] pcieport 0000:08:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[  120.345690] pcieport 0000:08:00.0: pci_hotplug: PCIe PME asserted
[  120.346001] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:08:00): 65, Channel: 00000001
[  120.346200] nvidia 0000:08:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

mike: interesting — network-shuffle correlation could point to interrupts or DMA storms. Which NICs are attached to those racks?

ana: Mellanox ConnectX-6 linked via 100G leafs. Switch telemetry looks fine. I ran a short netstress and saw bursts aligning w/ PX config updates.

cheng: can you run the cold-boot soak harness with repeated PCIe resets and the net-stress job? maybe the kernel driver ordering at boot is exposing a race. Suggested command: `soak-harness run --suite pci-reset,net-stress --duration 4h --targets g2 --reboot-mode cold --collect dmesg,nvml`

ana: starting that now on rack g2-rack-7 and g2-rack-8. tagging ops-bot to schedule longer window if we need it. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: scheduled soak job soak-2418004321-01 — 4h run on g2-rack-7,g2-rack-8, collection to s3://redwood-telemetry/soak/2418004321/. Notifying on completion.

mike: if we hit repro, let's try two quick mitigations: 1) pin the NIC driver to the earlier kernel init ordering (modprobe options), 2) boot with `pcie_aspm=off` just to isolate link state. If repro stops, we can formalize a kconfig workaround.

ana: agreed. I'll append a secondary job: `soak-harness run --suite pci-reset,net-stress --duration 2h --targets g2-rack-7 --kernel-args "pcie_aspm=off" --collect dmesg,nvml` after the baseline run.

sylvia: also recommend adding KV-cache-heavy inference load to emulate our real traffic — sometimes only combined GPU+network stress surfaces the flake. Jamal can help with a short synthetic load.

jamal: can do — I'll push a workload that streams 1k short requests/sec with 64-token generation. Will coordinate start time so we can correlate traces.

cheng: please include `traceid` headers so we can join traces between scheduler, NIC telemetry, and GPU NVML. Also enable perf counters around PCIe errors.

ana: will do. storing run configs in the soak run bucket. If the baseline shows no repro after 4h, we'll escalate to a warm-boot variant and then to wider fleet sample. If we repro, next steps: isolate driver version, collect pcr dump, and propose hotfix for Dedicated pools to avoid cold-rebooting these cards until patch lands.

mike: add cost note — 6h of targeted soak on two racks is ~0.8 reserved-GPU-days. ok for now but don't scale until we have actionable.

ana: noted. will post initial soak results in this thread when ops-bot finishes. thanks all. :wave:
